restatements.text: Reduces the state personal income tax rate from 6 percent to 5 percent of taxable income, effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2028.

findings.mechanism: Reduces the personal income tax rate to 5 percent.

findings.quote: the personal income tax rate is 5 percent
findings.mechanism: Reduces the tax rate on personal income, which lowers the amount of revenue collected by the state for public services.

analysis.answer: Current law sets the personal income tax rate at 6 percent. This measure reduces that rate to 5 percent starting in 2028.
The direct cost is the loss of state revenue resulting from the 1 percentage point decrease in the income tax rate. This will reduce funds available for the state budget.

Individuals and families who pay state income taxes will benefit from a lower tax bill. Those who rely on state-funded public services, or agencies that depend on state appropriations, will likely bear the cost of reduced revenues.

Taxpayers will have more disposable income. The state legislature and agencies will have to balance the budget by reducing spending on public services, drawing from reserves, or raising other revenues.

Whether reducing state income taxes stimulates enough economic growth to offset revenue losses is widely disputed among researchers. Some find that lower taxes attract investment and increase labor supply, while others find that cuts to public services offset any economic gains and that tax cuts primarily reduce overall revenues.
